text:
Calculate moles of acid and hydroxide:

- Acetic acid:  
  \[
  n_{\ce{CH3COOH}}=(0.500)(0.100)=0.050\ \text{mol}
  \]

- Hydrochloric acid:  
  \[
  n_{\ce{H+}}=(0.400)(0.200)=0.080\ \text{mol}
  \]

Total acid equivalents:
\[
n_{\text{acid}}=0.050+0.080=0.130\ \text{mol}
\]

Each mole of \(\ce{Ba(OH)2}\) supplies two moles of \(\ce{OH^-}\):

\[
n_{\ce{OH^-}}=2(0.300)(0.300)=0.180\ \text{mol}
\]

Thus, excess hydroxide is:

\[
n_{\ce{OH^-},\text{excess}}=0.180-0.130=0.050\ \text{mol}
\]

The total solution volume is:

\[
V_{\text{total}}=0.500+0.400+0.300=1.200\ \text{L}
\]

Therefore,

\[
[\ce{OH^-}]=\frac{0.050}{1.200}=0.04167\ \text{M}
\]

\[
\mathrm{pOH}=-\log(0.04167)=1.38
\]

\[
\mathrm{pH}=14.00-1.38=12.62
\]

Answer: C
